rationale: The target is a faithful concrete answer to an exercise whose mathematical task is intentionally under-specified at the formula level. It preserves the complete inherited probabilistic setting, ranges over every 0<p<2 including p<1, uses the source psi_2 maximum and Euclidean coefficient scale, and gives both comparison directions uniformly. The explicit reciprocal-power lower factor is exactly the kind of p-dependent result produced by modifying the cited extrapolation trick; a universal C absorbs the absolute constants from the p=3 Khintchine bound. The upper coefficient one is the standard L^p<=L^2 comparison on a probability space. Since the source asks the reader to select a version, these quantitative choices instantiate rather than genuinely strengthen a fixed printed proposition. Both implication directions therefore hold under the source's intended reading, with no unresolved dependency or semantic item.
